fullPassage: With respect to health, sometimes your mind can be your own worst enemy. If you are afflicted with illness anxiety, the fear of developing a disease or already being sick, you might devote countless hours to looking up symptoms, to the point where you start to believe that you are experiencing them, even if there is nothing physically wrong with you. Such a fear may arise if you know someone who has recently been diagnosed with the illness in question and therefore are aware of exactly what to expect or if you have suffered from the condition before and worry about it returning. Going to see a doctor may seem like the wisest course of action. After all, medical professionals can provide the reassurance you need. Ironically, though, a visit to the doctor can occasionally worsen the problem. In fact, you may be so preoccupied with the notion that you are sick and that the doctor has missed something that actual physiological effects can occur such as the release of substances in the body that cause headaches. In this way, illness anxiety can become a self-fulfilling prophecy.

det.tip: '때때로 악화될 수 있다'를 '항상 즉시 해결된다'로 뒤집는 오답 패턴에 유의

ch: 질병 불안은 병에 걸리거나 이미 아픈 것에 대한 두려움이다.

questions.passage: With respect to health, sometimes your mind can be your own worst enemy. If you are afflicted with illness anxiety, the fear of developing a disease or already being sick, you might devote countless hours to looking up symptoms, to the point where you start to believe that you are experiencing them, even if there is nothing physically wrong with you. Such a fear may arise if you know someone who has recently been diagnosed with the illness in question and therefore are aware of exactly what to expect or if you have suffered from the condition before and worry about it returning. Going to see a doctor may seem like the wisest course of action. After all, medical professionals can provide the reassurance you need. Ironically, though, a visit to the doctor can occasionally worsen the problem. In fact, you may be so preoccupied with the notion that you are sick and that the doctor has missed something that actual physiological effects can occur such as the release of substances in the body that cause headaches. In this way, illness anxiety can become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ①번은 원문과 불일치 — 신체적으로 아무 이상이 없어도 증상을 겪는다고 믿을 수 있다고 했으므로 '실제 이상이 있을 때만'은 사실과 다름
det.analysis:
① 불일치 — 원문은 even if there is nothing physically wrong with you(신체적 이상이 없어도)라 했으므로 '실제 이상이 있을 때만 느낀다'는 정반대 ←정답
② 일치 — Such a fear may arise if you know someone who has recently been diagnosed
③ 일치 — actual physiological effects can occur
④ 일치 — illness anxiety can become a self-fulfilling prophecy
det.tip: '이상이 없어도'를 '이상이 있을 때만'으로 조건을 뒤집는 오답에 유의

ch: 질병 불안이 있는 사람은 신체적으로 실제 이상이 있을 때만 증상을 느낀다.
아는 사람이 최근 그 병을 진단받았으면 질병 불안이 생길 수 있다.
아프다는 생각에 사로잡히면 실제 신체적 반응이 나타날 수 있다.
질병 불안은 자기충족적 예언이 될 수 있다.

det.korean: ② 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 provides가 아니라 provide로 써야 함

③ ✅ 적절 — 조동사 can 뒤 동사원형 worsen이 옳게 쓰임

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 조건에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로) 사실, 당신은 자신이 아프다는 생각과 그 의사가 무언가를 놓쳤다는 생각에 너무 사로잡힌 나머지 실제 생리적 반응이 일어날 수도 있다. In fact, you may be so preoccupied with the notion that you are sick and __________ that actual physiological effects can occur. (6단어)
[조건] (1) doctor, has, missed, something, that, the를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '그 의사가 무언가를 놓쳤다는'은 앞의 the notion과 병렬을 이루는 동격 that절이므로 that+주어(the doctor)+동사(has missed)+목적어(something) 순서로 배열해야 함
det.analysis: 앞의 'the notion that you are sick'과 and로 연결되는 두 번째 동격 that절이 필요함. 동격절은 '접속사 that + 주어 + 동사 + 목적어' 순서이므로 that the doctor has missed something이 됨. 주어 the doctor는 단수이므로 동사는 has missed(현재완료)로 쓰고, 그 목적어로 something을 둠
det.tip: the notion (that ...) and (that ...) 두 동격 that절의 병렬 구조 — that+S+V+O 어순에 유의
